question: In rheumatoid arthritis, achieving biological remission (DAS28 < 2.6) guarantees that the patient will report a satisfactory quality of life and return to their previous functional capacity.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is FALSE. DAS28 remission measures synovial inflammation, not the full biopsychosocial impact of RA. Patients in remission may still have persistent pain, depression, occupational disability, and impaired social functioning. Quality-of-life assessment using PROMs (HAQ-DI, PHQ-9, PROMIS) is required alongside disease activity measures.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — the statement is FALSE. Biological remission (DAS28 <2.6) does not guarantee patient-perceived quality-of-life remission. Many patients in DAS28 remission still report significant functional limitation (elevated HAQ-DI), depression, pain sensitisation, and work disability. Patient-reported outcomes and biopsychosocial assessment must be conducted alongside disease activity measures.
